items.title: China is the clear winner of Trump's trade war. While his tariffs succeeded in reducing the U.S. merchandise trade deficit with China, our overall goods trade deficit has barely improved, despite Americans paying higher prices. Meanwhile, China's overall goods surplus has soared.

items.title: The nickel and copper in modern nickels are now worth 7.76 cents, 55% more than the cost of buying nickels from the bank at face value. The U.S. government stopped making pennies last year. Soon it may stop making nickels too. Buy yours while you can. Much better than Treasuries.

items.title: Despite copper trading at a record high priced in dollars, priced in gold it's actually cheap. For the copper-to-gold ratio to get back to its historical average, copper must rise 60% to over $11 per pound. But gold won't stay at $4,400, so copper's rise could be much greater.

items.title: With copper at $6.85 per pound, the melt value of a pre-1982 penny is 4.46 cents. Even modern pennies, made mostly of zinc, have a current melt value of 1.07 cents. Pennies are a much better investment than Treasuries. They're not only risk-free, but the upside potential is huge.
